title: How Zach Yadegari built Cal AI to $1.4M/month at 18: AI photo calorie tracking and influencer marketing
summary: Zach Yadegari explains how he spotted a pain point in calorie tracking apps, used AI to remove the friction, and went all-in with his co-founders. He covers influencer marketing as Cal AI's core growth engine, reinvesting profits, and the cash-flow lag from Apple's payout schedule.

principles.text: Build around the friction that made you quit a competitor's product; AI removes the manual work.
principles.quote: the app required me to weigh my food on a scale, type in everything I was eating. It was unsustainable for my lifestyle.

principles.text: When early response to a launch is strongly positive, go all-in and commit full time.
principles.quote: The response immediately was very positive. That's when we knew we had something good on our hands and we decided to go allin.

principles.text: Influencer marketing is the special sauce, and most of the spend goes there.
principles.quote: Our special sauce at Cali, what we really do, right, is influencer marketing. And that's where a far majority of our spending goes to.

principles.text: Concentrated time with the team, first hires and a good rhythm can be the turning point.
principles.quote: we moved to San Francisco for the month of July. We stayed there for a month, lived in a hacker house, basically slept in the office

principles.text: Reinvest most revenue into the product and growth; pay dividends only from leftover cash.
principles.quote: We reinvest most of the money back into the app from Cali, but whenever there's enough cash left over, we will pay out dividends to ourselves.

principles.text: App store payout delays mean fast scaling can drain cash even when profitable; plan for the lag.
principles.quote: we were scaling faster than Apple was paying us, which meant that for months we were putting money in and weren't seeing a proportional amount of money out.
